content:
Harper (Finance): Flagging a true-up discrepancy for OmniHealth private deployment. Customer was migrated from Support Tier B -> Tier A mid-term and our annual true-up invoice (TUP-2026-33) appears to charge platform fee at Tier B rates for the entire year. They paid the charged amount but dispute the calculation.

Noah (Accounting): Paste of true-up calc attached by CS: 'Annual platform fee: Tier A $120k, Tier B $90k. Customer requested Tier A effective 2026-04-01. True-up billed: $90k (full year) - suggests migration not captured.'

Rina (Customer Success): Customer provided signed change order dated 2026-04-01 (CO-765). They expect true-up to prorate: charge Tier B for 01-03 then Tier A from 04 onward, net delta billed = (pro-rated Tier A amount - pro-rated Tier B amount).

billing-bot: True-up job TUP-JOB-2026-04 ran 2026-04-05. Source SKU tag for account shows last update 2026-04-01 03:12 UTC. Invoice TUP-2026-33 created 2026-04-06. Billing logic uses SKU tag as of job run time.

Omar (Sales): The CO was uploaded to Zendesk but our ops sync to billing didn't run until 04/02; looks like the database record kept old tier for one extra day. Customer insists the effective date is 04/01 and wants correction.

Tess (Legal): If CO effective date is 04/01 we should honor it. Recommend issuing an adjusting invoice (negative + replacement) and noting the credit reason as "support-tier effective date correction per CO-765". Also confirm no SLA or penalty language.

Harper (Finance): Agreed. Since this is an internal sync lag, propose: issue credit CN-2026-0038 for the overcharged amount, reissue corrected true-up invoice TUP-2026-33-R with prorated Tier A/B amounts, and automatically waive any finance fees. Approvals: Sales + Legal sign-off.

Noah (Accounting): Need calc: overcharge = $30,000 (difference full year) but prorated correction from 04/01 to 12/31 results in net extra charge for customer of $22,500. Current invoice billed $90,000; corrected true-up should be $112,500. So credit $90,000 and charge $112,500 -> net charge $22,500. But because customer already paid $90k, we should invoice for the $22,500 delta. Simpler: create invoice ADJ-2026-045 for $22,500 and mark previous as corrected.

Rina (Customer Success): Customer prefers single corrected invoice rather than separate debit. Can we issue a replacement invoice TUP-2026-33-R for $112,500 and apply payment to it, then credit the old one?

Harper (Finance): Yes that's cleaner. Accounting will create credit note CN-2026-0038 reversing TUP-2026-33, then new invoice TUP-2026-33-R for $112,500 and apply existing payment. Accounting confirm payment application will net zero refund.

Noah (Accounting): Confirmed. Will create CN-2026-0038, create TUP-2026-33-R for $112,500, apply payment. ETA 24h. Will include memo: "effective date correction per CO-765; replacing TUP-2026-33".

Omar (Sales): I'll notify the customer and attach CO-765 and timeline. Rina will loop in CS for post-payment reconciliation.

Harper (Finance): Also engineering note: ensure ops sync respects CO effective date and that true-up job looks at contract effective date, not catalog tag timestamp. Filed BILL-9088 for fix.

billing-bot: Ticket BILL-9088 created and assigned to eng-billing.

Rina (Customer Success): Customer acknowledged and thanked us for fast resolution. Leaving account note.

Noah (Accounting): Credit + replacement invoice created and payment re-applied. Closing thread.
